- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to prevent false optimism.  
- If forecast overshoots true value by >5% in early days of the 30d horizon, apply a 3–5 day lag correction by reducing the next 3–5 forecast points.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–1.0) and forecast is erratic, smooth the 30d curve by averaging 3–5 consecutive points to reduce noise.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 72.0) and forecast is still rising, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5 days.  
- For sentiment history with repeated 1.0 values, assume market is “overconfident” — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to reflect cooling sentiment.
